newsitem.title: GERMANY: Bonn's Schaeuble says no softening of EMU criteria.
newsitem.headline: Bonn's Schaeuble says no softening of EMU criteria.

text.p: Chancellor Helmut Kohl's powerful lieutenant Wolfgang Schaeuble said on Saturday Bonn would insist that there must be no softening of the economic criteria for EU Economic and Monetary Union (EMU).

Schaeuble, parliamentary leader of Kohl's Christian Democrats (CDU), told a conference in Berlin that the government would do everything in its power to ensure that the planned single currency came into force on January 1, 1999.

"The most important thing is that we should take this agreed step as it was set down in Maastricht (in the Treaty on European Union)," Schaeuble said, adding that the room for interpretation of this agreement was very slim.
Bonn was committed to ensuring that its 1997 budget deficit was below the stipulated three percent of gross domestic product, Schaeuble added.
